decision.reason: Retain mixref_initial scientifically unchanged as mixref_final. All three fixed initial deliveries succeeded and all 30 statistics per draw were reviewed. Analytically fitted biomarker margins, Pearson/Spearman association and OLS projections already target the admitted development sample estimates. Initial glycemic discrepancies change direction across seeds; finite-draw variation and tail sensitivity are more plausible than a stable offset to correct. Known BMI-quantile approximation and underidentified dependence assumptions remain explicit. Extra trials would not identify those missing relationships, and no seed-specific calibration or favorable-seed choice is justified.
addressed_findings: Verified all three executions and output links, all 90 statistic calculations and matched declared semantics, with zero nonpositive glycemia and duplicate measurement rows in each draw.
Separated small analytic BMI quantile mismatch from Monte Carlo variation; three BMI medians sit slightly above the reference, as the retained one-lognormal model predicts.

Examined regression coefficients and both glycemic correlations across every seed, preserving source-adjustment distinctions and refusing to treat reported reference confidence intervals as pass/fail or tuning targets.

Computed closed-form fourth-moment sampling scales for glucose/HbA1c SD and Pearson correlation to contextualize tail-sensitive variation. Calculations produce no synthetic rows and do not establish the model's scientific correctness.

Bound full initial delivery feedback and the prior actual trial feedback. Declined optional final-phase trials4301/4302 and preserved generator/spec/evidence bytes for required final delivery at all three fixed seeds.
remaining_limitations: Supplied CHNS summaries are selected-sample development estimates, not independent validation, population truth or national representation.
Component tail shapes and the assumed broad-component correlation, mixture-indicator independence from age/sex/BMI, nuisance covariate correlations and within-bin age shape remain underidentified.
BMI lognormal quantiles are approximate; no parameter-uncertainty or evidence-selection model is represented.
IID rows do not reproduce community clustering, survey weights, treatments, disease states, missingness or measurement rounding. Causal, prediction and subgroup uses remain unassessed.
External studies retain their own populations, selection, plasma/serum measures and adjustment/weighting. No source-context replay was provided; it remains not_computable.
Reusing identical generators and final seeds will reproduce the initial outputs; this retention is not a claimed numerical improvement or an additional validation sample.

reference_role: Declared development reference: consistency is not independent validation
uncertainty_policy: Reference sampling uncertainty is retained per statistic; three generation draws are conditional variation, not independent validation.

analytic_sampling_scale_context.method: Closed-form raw moments of the fitted four-component bivariate lognormal mixture, central-moment binomial expansion, delta-method sample-SD and Pearson influence-function variances; no sampling, no generator import.
analytic_sampling_scale_context.limits: First-order large-n conditional-model sampling scales, not exact finite-sample bounds, source uncertainty, validated clinical tolerances or hypothesis tests. Three fixed draws do not estimate structural uncertainty. Regression/Spearman MC uncertainty remains unestimated.
